heard: Male deep-sea anglerfish dissolve their bodies to survive. Starting with the scale of everyday fish, researchers found there are more than 200 species of anglerfish. Moving up the ladder, females use a bioluminescent lure on their heads to attract unsuspecting prey. These massive females can stretch their jaws and stomachs to swallow prey up to twice their own size. At the extreme end of the scale, female deep-sea anglerfish can grow up to 60 times the size of the tiny males. When a male finally encounters a female, he latches onto her using his teeth. Over time, the attached male physically fuses with the female, merging their blood vessels and skin. Male deep-sea anglerfish dissolve their bodies to survive.
